# Stop Biting
> An app that uses on-device AI (MediaPipe/WebAssembly) to detect nail biting (onychophagia) in real-time via webcam, then sounds an alarm. No camera data is sent anywhere while it runs. Available as a web app (PWA) that runs in any modern browser on a Mac or Windows computer with a webcam.

Every link below carries the page's own description, generated from the same source the page renders — see scripts/sync-seo.mjs. Stop Biting is a paid product and this site exists to sell it; the pages that compare it head-to-head with a competing app say so in their own opening paragraph. One person writes the site: Igor Gazivoda, a software developer, not a clinician.

Pricing:

- Free trial: 3 days, no credit card required — the full detector, streak tracking and incident history
- Monthly: $2.99/month
- Yearly: $29.00/year — about $2.42/month, 19% less than paying monthly
- Every plan includes unlimited AI detection, streak and habit tracking, full incident history, and all alert types (sound and visual)
- Payment is taken through Paddle, and a plan can be cancelled at any time

Key facts:

- Stop Biting runs MediaPipe models in WebAssembly on your own device — the camera feed never leaves it, and once the detection models have downloaded nothing carrying camera data is sent while it watches, which anyone can verify in a browser network monitor
- Detection works fully offline after the initial load; no camera data is transmitted or stored
- It detects nail biting using two MediaPipe models: a hand landmark model tracking 21 keypoints, and a face mesh tracking 468 facial landmarks
- Supported platforms: any modern browser with a webcam, as a no-install PWA, on Mac or Windows
- It detects nail biting only. Competing apps cover more behaviours, run on phones, or cost less, and the comparison pages below say where each of them beats us
- Nail biting (onychophagia) is estimated at 20–30% of the general population and up to 45% of children between age 10 and puberty (Lee & Lipner, Int J Environ Res Public Health, 2022). Both are review-level estimates inherited from earlier reviews rather than measurements, and single studies that measured it directly run lower and vary by population, so treat them as a range rather than a rate
- Habit Reversal Training is the best-studied treatment, which is not the same as having beaten every alternative: its only comparator in the landmark trial was negative practice, and it has never been tested against physical barriers at all. In that trial, participants' own daily episode counts fell by roughly 99% over five months, against about 60% for negative practice (Azrin, Nunn & Frantz, 1980). Five months is the study's duration, not a follow-up after treatment ended, and the counts were self-recorded by unblinded participants rather than measured by anyone else; the paper has no PubMed abstract and is paywalled, so those figures are quoted from Table 1 of the open-access Lee & Lipner review
- The durability evidence is a different trial: Twohig et al. (2003), placebo-controlled, in which nail length was 22% above baseline immediately after treatment and still 19% above baseline five months later, against 3% and 0% for placebo. The meta-analysis of 18 habit reversal studies covering 575 participants reports a large pooled effect, d = 0.80, but from pre-treatment to final post-treatment assessment, and pooled across six classes of repetitive behaviour rather than nail biting alone (Bate et al., Clinical Psychology Review, 2011)
- The DSM-5 classifies nail biting under "Other Specified Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorder" only when it reaches clinical severity; the vast majority of people who bite their nails would not meet the criteria for any disorder
- Competitor details are re-verified against each vendor's own website — and against the app store listing that site links to, when the two disagree — and every comparison page closes with a dated "How we verified this page" section stating when the check ran. Read the date on the page rather than trusting a date in this file

## Blog articles

### Treatment

- [Habit Reversal Training for Nail Biting: What It Is and How to Actually Do It](https://stopbiting.today/blog/habit-reversal-training-guide): In the landmark 1980 trial, participants' self-recorded biting episodes fell roughly 99% over five months.
- [Best Remedies to Stop Nail Biting: Every Method Ranked by Evidence](https://stopbiting.today/blog/best-nail-biting-remedies): Every nail biting remedy ranked by evidence: habit reversal first, then bitter polish, mindfulness and AI detection apps, and what each can and cannot do.
- [Stopping Nail Biting for Good: What Relapses Mean and How to Build Lasting Change](https://stopbiting.today/blog/stopping-nail-biting-for-good): New habits took 18 to 254 days to become automatic in Lally's 2010 study, median 66 (not a nail-biting figure).
- [How Long Does It Take to Stop Nail Biting? A Realistic Timeline](https://stopbiting.today/blog/how-long-to-stop-nail-biting): In the one trial with a real follow-up, treated nail length was 22% above baseline at the end and 19% above five months later, against 3% and 0% for placebo.
- [Bitter Nail Polish for Nail Biting: Does It Work? A Review of the Evidence](https://stopbiting.today/blog/bitter-nail-polish-review): In a six-week trial of 80 nail biters, bitter polish had a 26% drop-out rate against 12% for a wristband, but did better among those who kept applying it.
- [How to Stop Nail Biting Fast: The Quickest Methods, Ranked by Evidence](https://stopbiting.today/blog/stop-nail-biting-fast): Nothing stops an established habit in days.
- [Does Hypnotherapy for Nail Biting Work? What the Research Actually Shows](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-hypnosis): Hypnotherapy for nail biting has no large controlled trials, only case reports and uncontrolled series.
- [What to Do Instead of Biting Your Nails: 12 Evidence-Based Alternatives](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-alternatives): Competing responses only work when they meet the same need as nail biting.
- [Can Acrylic Nails Stop Nail Biting? What Actually Happens When You Get Extensions](https://stopbiting.today/blog/acrylics-to-stop-nail-biting): Acrylic nails are one of the most popular ways to stop nail biting.
- [Is There a Permanent Cure for Nail Biting? An Honest Look at What the Evidence Shows](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-cure): The one trial with a five-month follow-up held its gains: nail length 22% above baseline at treatment end and 19% at follow-up, against 3% and 0% for placebo.
- [Stop Nail Biting in 30 Days: A Week-by-Week Plan](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-30-day-plan): We found no published data pinning down which weeks of practice give the steepest drop, so 30 days is a review point, not a finish line.
- [Fidget Toys for Nail Biting: Which Competing Responses Actually Work](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-fidget-toys): Fidget toys are popular competing responses for nail biting, but most don't work.
- [How to Stop Nail Biting Before Interviews and High-Pressure Situations](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-interview-anxiety): Nail biting spikes before interviews and presentations.
- [Tracking Your Nail Biting: Why Data Beats Willpower](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-habit-tracking): Tracking is the foundation of habit reversal, but in both controlled comparisons that tested self-monitoring alone it produced no significant nail-length gain.
- [How to Stop Nail Biting: The Complete Guide (2026)](https://stopbiting.today/blog/how-to-stop-nail-biting): Habit Reversal Training has the strongest evidence: self-recorded biting episodes fell roughly 99% over five months in the 1980 trial.
- [Can a Night Guard Stop Nail Biting? What Dentists Say](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-night-guard): Night guards are sometimes suggested for nighttime nail biting and grinding.
- [CBT for Nail Biting: How Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Helps](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-cognitive-behavioral-therapy): CBT for nail biting targets the thought patterns behind the habit, not just the behaviour.
- [What Actually Worked for People Who Quit Nail Biting, According to Online Communities](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-reddit): Across three BFRB self-help techniques, four-week completion ran 53.5% to 68.6%, so sticking with one is hard.
- [30-Day Nail Biting Challenge: A Day-by-Day Guide](https://stopbiting.today/blog/stop-nail-biting-challenge): A day-by-day guide to the 30-day stop nail biting challenge: specific daily actions, milestones to hit, and how to handle the days you don't stick to it.
- [Can a Gel Manicure Stop Nail Biting? What to Expect](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-gel-manicure): Gel deters rather than interrupts: a coating removes the ragged edges that start episodes, but not a bite on contact.
- [What Nail Technicians Wish Clients Knew About Nail Biting](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-nail-technicians): Nail technicians see chronic nail biting constantly.
- [Can Press-On Nails Stop Nail Biting? A Practical Look](https://stopbiting.today/blog/press-on-nails-to-stop-nail-biting): Press-ons deter the way acrylics do (harder to bite through, different under the teeth) and cost far less.
- [Essential Oils for Nail Biting: Do DIY Bitter Remedies Work?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-essential-oils): Neem oil can work on the same aversive principle as bitter polish; the difference is durability, since it washes off faster.
- [Magnesium for Nail Biting: Can It Help With Anxiety-Driven Biting?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-magnesium): No trial has tested magnesium for nail biting.
- [Nail Biting Support Groups and Communities: What Helps and What Does Not](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-support-groups): Across three BFRB self-help techniques, four-week completion ran 53.5% to 68.6%, and they worked to the extent people kept using them.
- [Mindfulness for Nail Biting: Useful, Oversold, and Frequently Misapplied](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-mindfulness): In 72 nail biters, decoupling beat relaxation on withstanding the urge, at trend level only on symptoms.
- [Trigger Mapping: Find Out When You Actually Bite Your Nails](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-trigger-mapping): Most people are wrong about when they bite their nails.
- [Habit Stacking for Nail Biting: Attaching New Responses to Existing Cues](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-habit-stacking): Habit stacking works well for building new routines, but nail biting needs a specific variant.
- [Using an Accountability Partner to Stop Nail Biting](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-accountability-partner): Social support is a formal component of habit reversal training and the one most people skip.
- [A Nail Care Routine Built for People Who Bite](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-care-routine-for-nail-biters): Fingernails regrow at about 3.47 mm a month, measured in 22 healthy young adults.
- [How to Choose a Nail Biting Treatment: A Decision Framework](https://stopbiting.today/blog/how-to-choose-nail-biting-treatment): Habit reversal has the best evidence: self-recorded episodes fell roughly 99% over five months in the original trial.
- [The 5 Biggest Mistakes People Make When Trying to Stop Nail Biting](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-mistakes): Most failed attempts at stopping nail biting fail in the same five ways.
- [Nail Biting by Situation: What Changes for Children, Musicians, Nurses and Desk Workers](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-by-situation): The method does not change from person to person.
- [Does Snapping a Rubber Band Stop Nail Biting? What the Trials Tested](https://stopbiting.today/blog/rubber-band-snap-nail-biting): No trial found tested snapping a rubber band for nail biting.
- [Acceptance and Commitment Therapy for Nail Biting: What the Evidence Covers](https://stopbiting.today/blog/acceptance-commitment-therapy-nail-biting): No trial found tested acceptance and commitment therapy for nail biting.
- [Inositol for Nail Biting: Is There Any Evidence?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/inositol-nail-biting): No trial found tested inositol for nail biting.
- [Online Therapy for Nail Biting: What the Studies Show](https://stopbiting.today/blog/online-therapy-nail-biting): No trial has tested online therapy for nail biting alone.
- [Stimulus Control for Nail Biting: Changing What Sets It Off](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-stimulus-control): Stimulus control is first-line for hair pulling and skin picking.
- [Does Chewing Gum Stop Nail Biting? What the Evidence Shows](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-chewing-gum): No study has tested chewing gum for nail biting.
- [Does Keeping Your Nails Short or Filed Stop Nail Biting?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-short-nails-trimming): No trial has tested trimming or filing alone for nail biting.

### Psychology

- [Why Do People Bite Their Nails, and Why Is It So Hard to Stop?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/why-do-people-bite-their-nails): Reviews estimate 20–30% of adults bite their nails, and up to 45% of children between 10 and puberty.
- [The Stress–Nail Biting Connection: Why Anxiety Drives the Habit and How to Break the Loop](https://stopbiting.today/blog/stress-and-nail-biting): In 339 medical students, 65.7% of nail biters reported tension before biting and 42% pleasure after: self-report, not measured relief.
- [Nail Biting and Anxiety: When Treating Anxiety Is the Key to Stopping the Habit](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-anxiety-treatment): In 339 medical students, anxiety disorder was diagnosed in 22.5% of those with lifetime nail biting against 26.2% of those without.
- [Why Nail Biting Persists into Adulthood, and What Makes It Different to Childhood Habits](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-adults-why-persists): In a survey of 4,335 college students, body-focused repetitive behaviours tended to be chronic, lasting over a year.
- [Nail Biting and ADHD: Why the Habit Is Harder to Stop, and What Actually Helps](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-adhd): In a psychiatrically referred sample of nail-biting children, 74.6% also had ADHD, the most common co-occurring diagnosis.
- [Why Nail Biting Feels Calming: The Emotional Regulation Mechanism Explained](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-emotional-regulation): In 339 medical students, 65.7% of nail biters reported tension before biting and 42% pleasure after: self-report, not physiology.
- [The Social Cost of Nail Biting: How Stopping Changes More Than Just Your Nails](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-social-confidence): In 3,475 Turkish students, quality-of-life scores were lower in those with nail biting than in those without.
- [Nail Biting in Teenagers: What the Evidence Actually Shows](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-teenagers): No source we could find locates a peak age.
- [Nail Biting and Perfectionism: What the Evidence Actually Shows](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-and-perfectionism): The perfectionism link rests on one study of 24 people that used no perfectionism scale: boredom and frustration raised urges, and a stress induction did not.
- [Nail Biting While Gaming: Why It Happens and How to Stop](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-gaming): In a randomised experiment, 40 undergraduate nail biters bit most when left alone and when working maths problems.
- [What Your Nail Biting Says About Your Personality](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-personality): Nail biting correlates with perfectionism, anxiety sensitivity and sensation seeking, but the perfectionism link rests on one study of 24 people.
- [Why You Bite Your Nails More at Night: The Science Explained](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-evening): No time-of-day prevalence data has been published.
- [Men and Nail Biting: Why It's Underreported and What Actually Helps](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-men): No reliable sex difference has been shown: 28% of boys vs 26% of girls in 1,131 twin pairs, 20.1% vs 24.4% in 743 schoolchildren.
- [How Phones and Screens Make Nail Biting Worse, and What to Do](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-screen-time): Screen time and nail biting have not been studied together in large-scale research.
- [Nail Biting and Depression: Is There a Connection?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-and-depression): In 603 adults with OCD, the 52 who also bit their nails had depressive scores no different from those who did not.
- [How Severe Is Your Nail Biting? A Self-Assessment](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-quiz): A short, evidence-informed nail biting self-assessment covering frequency, damage, and triggers.
- [Nail Biting During Exams: Why Stress Season Makes It Worse](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-during-exams): In four conditions, 40 undergraduate biters bit most when left alone and on maths problems: better evidenced triggers than stress.
- [Why 'Stop Biting My Nails' Resolutions Fail, and What Works Instead](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-new-years-resolution): In 339 medical students, 92.2% of nail biters described their own behaviour as automatic, which is why willpower resolutions fail.
- [Nail Biting in College: Why Dorm Life Makes It Worse](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-college-students): Prevalence data show no college peak: 17.6% of university students against 29.2% of high schoolers in a 3,475-student Turkish survey.
- [Why Nail Biting Increases After Quitting Smoking](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-after-quitting-smoking): We have not found a study tracking nail biting before and after quitting smoking.
- [Nail Biting Before Public Speaking: Why Performance Anxiety Triggers It](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-public-speaking): In 24 people with a BFRB and 23 controls, urges rose under boredom and frustration but not stress.
- [Does Caffeine Make Nail Biting Worse?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-caffeine): Nobody has studied caffeine and nail biting together, and the arousal premise is shaky: a stress induction failed to raise urges where boredom did.
- [Nail Biting and Alcohol: Why Drinking Can Increase the Habit](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-alcohol): In 339 medical students, 92.2% of biters called the habit automatic.
- [How to Help a Partner or Friend Who Bites Their Nails (Without Nagging)](https://stopbiting.today/blog/how-to-help-someone-who-bites-their-nails): In the only experiment we found, 40 undergraduate biters bit least when watched in conversation or reprimanded.
- [Nail Biting in Women: Patterns, Pressures, and What Helps](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-women): No reliable sex difference has been shown: a twin study found biting by age 12 in 28% of boys and 26% of girls.
- [Why You Bite Your Nails More on Flights and While Traveling](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-flights-travel): Airport dead time beats flight nerves on evidence: 40 undergraduate nail biters bit most when left alone, and a mood induction found no increase under stress.
- [Is Nail Biting Contagious Among Friends and Partners?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-contagious): Family clustering has been measured; social spread has not.
- [Nail Biting During Major Life Changes: Job Loss, Moving, Breakups, and Grief](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-major-life-changes): Stress is the weakest-evidenced part of this.
- [Boredom Biting: Why an Empty Moment Sends Your Hand to Your Mouth](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-boredom): Four conditions: 40 undergraduate biters bit most when bored or frustrated, least in conversation or reprimand.
- [Is Nail Biting an Oral Fixation? What That Idea Gets Right and Wrong](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-oral-fixation): A survey of 281 pediatric patients put median onset at 5 years, range 1 to 13, mostly well after the proposed oral stage.
- [Ten Nail Biting Myths That Make It Harder to Stop](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-myths): Anxiety disorder was found in 22.5% of lifetime nail biters against 26.2% of non-biters in one 339-student survey.
- [Famous Nail Biters: The Habit Is More Common at the Top Than You Think](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-famous-people): The 20–30% figure is inherited from older reviews, not measured.
- [Nail Biting at the Gym and During Sports: What Helps and What Backfires](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-gym-sports): Almost nobody bites mid-workout.
- [Why Do I Bite My Nails Without Noticing? The Subconscious Habit Explained](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-subconscious-habit): Most nail biting runs on autopilot, which is why willpower fails.
- [Is Nail Biting a Form of Self-Harm?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/is-nail-biting-self-harm): By the usual definitions, no: nail biting is a body-focused repetitive behavior.
- [Is Nail Biting a Mental Disorder? What the Classification Says](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-mental-disorder): Most nail biting is a habit, not a diagnosis.
- [The Urge Before the Bite: What Is a Premonitory Urge?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-premonitory-urge): No study has measured the premonitory urge in nail biting.
- [Urge Surfing for Nail Biting: What the Evidence Shows](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-urge-surfing): No study has tested urge surfing for nail biting.
- [Shame and Nail Biting: Does Self-Criticism Make It Worse?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-shame-self-compassion): Shame raised the urge to bite in a small BFRB experiment.

### Health

- [The Real Health Risks of Nail Biting: What Nail Biting Actually Does to Your Body](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-health-risks): Enterobacteriaceae turned up in the saliva of 76% of 25 chronic nail biters against 26.5% of 34 non-biters.
- [Nail Biting During Sleep: Does It Happen and What Can You Do?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-during-sleep): We could not find a study measuring sleep nail biting: no prevalence figure, no sleep-stage data, no waking comparison.
- [Nail Biting During Pregnancy: What the Real Risks Are and How to Stop](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-pregnancy): Under the nail was the densest bacterial site on the hand in the classic 26-adult survey.
- [How to Grow Your Nails After Nail Biting: Timeline, Care Guide, and What to Expect](https://stopbiting.today/blog/grow-nails-after-nail-biting): Fingernails grow at a measured rate, not to a timeline: 3.47mm a month on average in 22 healthy young adults.
- [What Lives Under Your Fingernails: The Real Germ Risk of Nail Biting](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-bacteria-parasites): Enterobacteriaceae were found in the saliva of 76% of 25 chronic nail biters against 26.5% of 34 non-biters: a difference in detection, not a traced transfer.
- [Does Nail Biting Weaken Your Immune System?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-immune-system): No solid evidence that nail biting weakens immunity in a generally healthy person.
- [Nail Biting and Gut Health: What Swallowing Bacteria Does to Your Microbiome](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-gut-health): Research linking nail biting to microbiome disruption is limited.
- [Nail Biting with Braces: Why It's Worse and What to Do](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-braces): In 21 severe nail biters against 21 matched orthodontic patients, root resorption was higher before and after treatment, direction unproven.
- [Cuticle Damage from Nail Biting: What Happens and How to Repair It](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-cuticle-damage): Cuticle tissue regenerates, but only once biting stops; repair cannot outpace an active habit.
- [Nail Biting and Eczema: How the Two Conditions Interact](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-eczema): Eczema around the nails and nail biting can worsen each other in a specific feedback loop.
- [Nail Biting During Menopause: Why Hormonal Changes Can Trigger It](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-menopause): No study has looked at menopause and nail biting, or measured stress, sleep or mood against biting frequency.
- [Nail Biting Risks for Healthcare Workers: What to Know](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-healthcare-workers): We found no study on nail biting infection risk in any occupation.
- [Does Nail Biting Cause Permanent Damage? What's Reversible and What Isn't](https://stopbiting.today/blog/does-nail-biting-cause-permanent-damage): Most damage is reversible: the plate regrows about 3.47 mm a month for fingernails.
- [Do People Bite Their Toenails? Yes. Here's What to Know](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-toenails): The standard review says biting usually occurs in the fingernails, as toenails are rarely bitten.
- [Nail Biting for Chefs and Food Service Workers: The Hygiene Stakes](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-chefs-food-service): Some food codes bar artificial nails: a potential pathogen grew from 87% of healthcare workers with acrylics against 43% of controls, not in greater quantity.
- [Nail Biting in Older Adults: A Less-Discussed Pattern](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-seniors-elderly): Nail growth slows with age on thin evidence: one physician measured his own thumbnail for 35 years, 0.123 mm a day at 32, 0.095 at 67.
- [Can Birth Control Affect Nail Biting?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-birth-control): Hormonal birth control shifts the hormonal environment behind mood and stress reactivity.
- [Why Nail Biting Gets Worse in Winter](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-dry-skin-winter): Cold, dry air worsens the cuticle damage and rough edges that trigger nail biting.
- [Nail Biting and Fungal Infections: What to Know](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-fungal-infection): Yeasts grew from the subungual space of 69.0% of 26 ordinary adults: colonisation, not infection.
- [Paronychia: The Infection Nail Biters Get Most Often](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-paronychia): Acute paronychia is one of the most common hand infections, and nail biting is a listed risk factor.
- [Nail Biting and Warts: What the Evidence Actually Shows](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-warts): Beta-HPV DNA turned up in 61.1% of 185 fingernail samples, but those are cutaneous types, not wart types, and the authors cannot tell infection from deposition.
- [Nail Biting and Jaw Pain: The TMJ Connection](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-jaw-pain-tmj): In 240 adolescents, nail biting was significantly associated with TMD signs and symptoms (p = 0.001).
- [Hangnails and Nail Biting: The Trigger Loop Nobody Warns You About](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-hangnails): Hangnails are both a consequence of nail biting and one of its most reliable triggers.
- [White Spots on Bitten Nails: What They Are and What They Are Not](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-white-spots): White marks are conventionally attributed to matrix trauma, not a calcium or zinc lack.
- [Is Nail Biting a Sign of Vitamin Deficiency?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-vitamin-deficiency): No evidence links nail biting to a mineral deficiency.
- [Does Nail Biting Damage Your Teeth? What Has Actually Been Measured](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-teeth-damage): Less is measured than articles claim: one study on root resorption, one disputed on malocclusion, one on jaw signs.
- [What Happens If You Swallow Your Fingernails?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/swallowing-fingernails): We found no study of what swallowed nail clippings do.
- [Can You Get Pinworms From Biting Your Nails? What the Studies Show](https://stopbiting.today/blog/pinworm-nail-biting): Studies link nail biting to pinworm in children, but only as an association.
- [Staph, MRSA and Nail Biting: What the Studies Found](https://stopbiting.today/blog/staph-mrsa-nail-biting): No study measured staph carriage in nail biters.
- [Can Nail Biting Cause Cancer? What the Studies Show](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-cancer): No study shows nail biting causes cancer.
- [Dark Line on a Bitten Nail: Habit Mark or Something to Check?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-dark-line-on-nail): Nail biting can rarely cause a dark band on a nail, but so can melanoma.
- [Ridges and Grooves in Bitten Nails: Habit-Tic, Beau's Lines or Something Else?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-nail-ridges-grooves): Ridges and grooves are common in bitten nails, but not every groove comes from biting.
- [Does Nail Biting Spread Colds, Flu or Norovirus?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-colds-flu-norovirus): No study links nail biting to colds, flu or norovirus.

### Clinical

- [Nail Biting and OCD: Understanding the Link Between Nail Biting and Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-ocd-connection): The DSM-5 files clinically severe nail biting under Other Specified Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorder: near OCD, not OCD.
- [Nail Biting vs Skin Picking: How These Habits Compare and What Works for Each](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-vs-skin-picking): Nail biting and skin picking are both BFRBs with different triggers and treatments.
- [Nail Biting as Stimming: When the Habit Is Really Sensory Regulation](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-stimming): Adults with clinical-level BFRBs (n=26) reported more sensory sensitivity than subclinical and control groups.
- [Onychophagia: The Medical Term for Nail Biting, Explained](https://stopbiting.today/blog/onychophagia): Onychophagia is the clinical term for chronic nail biting.
- [Body-Focused Repetitive Behaviors (BFRBs): The Complete Guide](https://stopbiting.today/blog/bfrb-guide): Habit reversal pooled a large effect (d = 0.80) over 18 studies and 575 participants, across six behaviour classes, not nail biting alone.
- [Nail Biting and Autism: Understanding the Sensory Connection](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-autism): Nail biting is more common among autistic people, often serving sensory regulation rather than anxiety.
- [When to See a Doctor About Nail Biting (And Which Kind)](https://stopbiting.today/blog/when-to-see-a-doctor-for-nail-biting): Most nail biting doesn't need a doctor.
- [Nail Biting and Panic Disorder: When Biting Clusters Around Panic Attacks](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-panic-disorder): For some people with panic disorder, nail biting clusters around panic attacks rather than general anxiety.
- [Nail Biting and PTSD: Understanding the Hypervigilance Connection](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-ptsd): For some people with PTSD, nail biting is tied to hypervigilance and nervous system dysregulation rather than ordinary stress.
- [Dermatophagia: When You Bite the Skin, Not the Nail](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-dermatophagia): Many people who think they bite their nails actually bite the skin around them.
- [Is There Medication for Nail Biting? What the Evidence Says](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-medication): A 2023 evidence map screened 2,618 psychodermatology studies and found exactly two randomised drug trials for nail biting.
- [How to Find a Therapist Who Actually Treats Nail Biting](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-finding-a-therapist): The common failure is a therapist treating the biting as an anxiety symptom and working only on that.
- [Nail and Cuticle Picking (Onychotillomania): What It Is and What Helps](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-and-cuticle-picking): Nail picking is a body-focused repetitive behavior, like nail biting.
- [Is Nail Biting a Tic? Nail Biting vs Tics and Tourette Syndrome](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-vs-tics-tourette): Nail biting is a body-focused repetitive behaviour, not a tic, though the two can overlap.

### Science

- [Why Habits Are So Hard to Break, and What That Means for Nail Biting](https://stopbiting.today/blog/breaking-any-habit-science): Lally's 2010 study: the 39 whose data fitted the model took a median 66 days to reach 95% of the automaticity plateau, range 18 to 254.
- [Is Nail Biting Genetic? What the Research Says About Hereditary Habit Risk](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-genetics): In 1,131 pairs of 12-year-old Japanese twins, 50% of the variance in nail biting was attributed to genes.
- [NAC for Nail Biting: What N-Acetylcysteine Can and Can't Do](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nac-nail-biting): In a trial of 42 children and adolescents, NAC at 800mg/day significantly increased nail length at one month but not at two.
- [Nail Biting Statistics: How Common Is It, Really? (2026 Data)](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-statistics): Reviews estimate 20–30% of adults and up to 45% of children aged 10 to puberty bite their nails.
- [Nail Biting and Cortisol: The Stress Hormone Connection Explained](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-cortisol): No study we found has measured cortisol and nail biting together.
- [Does Nail Biting Affect Your Fingerprints?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-fingerprints): Ridges are templated in the dermis and regrow after surface wear, so ordinary biting leaves them intact.
- [Why Do Humans Bite Their Nails? An Evolutionary Perspective](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-evolutionary-psychology): Self-directed grooming is described across mammals, but none of that literature studied human nail biting.
- [Nail Biting and Dopamine: Why the Habit Rewards Itself](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-dopamine): Nail biting persists because it is reinforced, not because you lack discipline.
- [Which Fingers Do Nail Biters Bite Most, and Why It Is Not Random](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-which-fingers): Nobody appears to have published which fingers get bitten most, so this is report, not ranking.

### Comparison

- [5 Best Tools to Stop Nail Biting in 2026, Ranked by Evidence](https://stopbiting.today/blog/best-apps-to-stop-nail-biting): Ranked by evidence, not marketing: AI detection apps, bitter polish, reminder bands and habit trackers.
- [Stop Biting vs Mavala Stop: AI Detection vs Bitter Polish (2026)](https://stopbiting.today/blog/stop-biting-vs-mavala-stop): Mavala Stop uses bitter taste to deter nail biting.
- [Nail Biting vs Pen Chewing: Are They the Same Habit?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-vs-pen-chewing): Pen chewing and nail biting look similar but differ in mechanism and risk.
- [Nail Biting vs Hair Pulling: How These Two BFRBs Compare](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-vs-hair-pulling): Nail biting and hair pulling (trichotillomania) are both BFRBs but differ in visibility, treatment, and evidence base.
- [Nail Biting App vs Therapy: Which Is Right for You?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-app-vs-therapy): Detection apps and professional therapy both treat nail biting, but differ in cost, access, and intensity.
- [Nail Biting vs Knuckle Cracking: Comparing Two Common Habits](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-knuckle-cracking): Knuckle cracking and nail biting are both repetitive hand habits that work very differently.
- [Nail Biting vs Cheek and Lip Biting: Same Family, Different Problems](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-vs-cheek-biting): Cheek and lip biting share drivers with nail biting and frequently substitute for it.
- [Nail Biting vs Teeth Grinding: Two Habits, One Jaw](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-vs-teeth-grinding): Nail biting and bruxism share drivers and frequently occur together.

### Technology

- [How AI Can Help You Stop Biting Your Nails: The Technology Behind Real-Time Detection](https://stopbiting.today/blog/how-ai-can-help-stop-nail-biting): Real-time AI detection solves the awareness problem behind nail biting.
- [Is It Safe to Use a Webcam App to Stop Nail Biting? Privacy Explained](https://stopbiting.today/blog/webcam-privacy-nail-biting-app): Webcam apps for nail biting raise fair privacy questions.
- [How MediaPipe AI Detection Works in Stop Biting: A Technical Explainer](https://stopbiting.today/blog/mediapipe-ai-detection-explained): Stop Biting runs Google's MediaPipe in WebAssembly: a 21-point hand model and a 468-point face mesh, on your device five times a second.
- [Wearable Technology for Nail Biting: Smartwatches and Motion Detection](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-wearable-technology): Wrist-worn wearables are an emerging way to catch nail biting through motion sensing.
- [How Accurate Is AI Nail Biting Detection? A Straight Answer](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-detection-accuracy): It detects fingertip-to-mouth proximity, not teeth on a nail: five frames a second, three consecutive positives, about 600 milliseconds, before an alert fires.
- [Getting Your Camera Setup Right for Nail Biting Detection](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-camera-setup): Detection quality depends more on lighting and camera angle than on hardware.
- [Does Running Nail Biting Detection Slow Down Your Computer?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-app-battery-performance): Inference runs five times a second, not sixty, roughly a twelvefold cut in compute, at about 640 by 480, with no video uploaded.

### Products

- [Stop Biting App Review: An Honest Walkthrough From the Team That Built It](https://stopbiting.today/blog/stop-biting-app-review): Stop Biting uses on-device AI to catch nail biting in real time.
- [Products to Stop Nail Biting: A Complete Buyer's Guide](https://stopbiting.today/blog/products-to-stop-nail-biting): From bitter polish to fidget rings to AI apps: a categorised guide to products that stop nail biting, and what's actually worth buying for your pattern.
- [The Real Cost of Nail Biting: What Chronic Biting Costs Over Time](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-cost): Nail biting has a real financial cost: dental repairs, manicures, damaged devices, and more.
- [Can You Use FSA or HSA Funds for Nail Biting Treatment?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-fsa-hsa): Bitter polish, detection apps, and other nail biting treatments may qualify for FSA or HSA reimbursement.
- [Do Gloves Stop Nail Biting? An Honest Assessment](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-gloves): Gloves and finger covers are the most-suggested physical barrier for nail biting.
- [Tape, Plasters and Finger Covers for Nail Biting](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-finger-tape): Taping target fingers is cheap, discreet, and more sustainable than gloves.
- [Does Regular Nail Polish Help You Stop Biting?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-regular-nail-polish): Ordinary nail polish has no bitter agent and no real barrier, yet many biters report it helps.

### Parenting

- [Nail Biting in Kids: When It's Normal, When to Step In, and What Actually Helps](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-in-children): Clinical reviews estimate up to 45% of children between age 10 and puberty bite their nails.
- [Nail Biting in Toddlers: What's Normal at Ages 2–4](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-toddler): Parents reported nail biting in 23% of 3- to 6-year-olds in a small US interview study: common, not a precise rate.
- [From Thumb Sucking to Nail Biting: How One Habit Becomes the Other](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-thumb-sucking): In 1,131 pairs of 12-year-old Japanese twins, finger-sucking and nail biting co-occurred in 17.7% of males and 15.7% of females.
- [If You Bite Your Nails, Should You Hide It From Your Kids?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-parents-modeling): In 743 schoolchildren, 36.8% of biters had a family member who bit too, but a twin study put 50% of the variance on genes.
- [Why Punishing a Child for Nail Biting Backfires](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-punishing-children): In a randomised experiment, 40 undergraduate biters bit least in conversation and when reprimanded.
- [Reward Charts for a Child's Nail Biting: What Evidence Exists](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-reward-chart-children): No study has tested reward charts for children's nail biting.

### Productivity

- [Nail Biting During Deep Focus: Why Concentration Triggers the Habit](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-during-focus-and-work): Many people bite their nails during deep focus: coding, writing, reading.
- [How to Stop Nail Biting at Work and in Meetings: A Practical Professional's Guide](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-at-work-meetings): Nail biting during meetings, video calls, and presentations is hard to control.
- [Nail Biting for Musicians: Why It's a Bigger Problem Than for Most](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-musicians): For guitarists, pianists, and other instrumentalists, nail biting directly affects technique and tone.
- [Nail Biting for Teachers: Managing It in Front of a Classroom](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-teachers): Teachers face unique nail biting triggers: constant visibility, classroom stress, little downtime.

### Humor

- [You're Biting Your Nails Again. Your Laptop Saw the Whole Thing.](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-laptop-working-from-home): A funny, honest look at why working on a laptop turns even calm, rational adults into compulsive nail biters, and how AI detection can finally break the cycle.
